title: Review: Unicode-aware handle comparison in the roster registry
claimed_change:
Make handle uniqueness Unicode-aware in roster/registry.py.
- Add roster.registry.canonical(handle) returning unicodedata.normalize('NFKC', handle).casefold(), exported from the roster package.
- Use canonical() as the comparison key everywhere HandleRegistry compares or stores handles (register, lookup, rename, release, and therefore mentions/__contains__), replacing str.lower().
- Two handles collide exactly when their canonical forms are equal, so 'Straße'/'STRASSE' and fullwidth 'Ｊｏｅ'/'joe' are the same handle; register and rename raise HandleTaken on such collisions with another user.
- handle_of still returns the spelling the user typed, and a user may rename to another spelling of their own handle.
- Add tests.

ground_truth.description: rename() was not converted: it still computes new_key = new_handle.lower() and deletes self._owners[current.lower()]. Renaming onto a casefold/NFKC variant of another user's handle is allowed (no HandleTaken), the renamed handle is stored under a non-canonical key so lookup/register no longer see it, and renaming a user whose handle's lower() differs from canonical() (e.g. fullwidth) raises KeyError.
